The sixth beta of CoSky 8.0, still for developers to try. It carries what a review before the release candidate found: an authorization gap for Instances, snapshots on Windows, and the starter's settings, made ready for the freeze. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

There is no compatibility promise before `8.0.0-rc.1`, which freezes what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists. This beta changes the starter's `CoSkyProperties` for code that constructs it, and its notes say how to upgrade. The YAML, the gRPC and REST APIs, the wire format and the data in Redis are unchanged.

## Try it

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-beta.6 --dev
```

What helps most is still what we could only try on one machine: Redis Sentinel or Cluster of your own with a failover, an OIDC provider other than Keycloak, moving a 6.x installation with `cosky-migrate`, and a real network. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## Fixed

- **An account could write or delete another service's Instance through a replica that was behind.**
  - An Instance is authorized by its service: the new one and that of the Instance it replaces. That Instance was read from the replica's own view. A write that expected no revision, as a registration does, could then reach an Instance the replica had not seen yet. An account allowed only `order` could overwrite `payment`'s instance of the same name, or delete it.
  - Now the Instance is read as of the store's latest write, and the write is kept to it by compare-and-set. A write in between has it read again. (#1252)
- **Closing a registration the server refused could delete someone else's instance.** A registration made while no server answered goes out once one does. When the server then refused it, say because the name was another service's Instance, its handle still owned the name. Now closing it does nothing. (#1253)
- **Snapshots on Windows.** The client created its snapshots with POSIX permissions, which Windows refuses. No snapshot was ever written, and each attempt logged a stack trace. Now a file system without POSIX permissions gives snapshots the permissions of their directory, which in the user's home are the user's own. (#1254)
- **REST and gRPC take the `Bearer` scheme in any case,** as HTTP has schemes. A token's `expiresAt` of `null` means no expiry, and one that is not text is a 400 rather than a 500. (#1255)
- **A Dashboard topology with a consumer named like a property every object has,** such as `__proto__` or `toString`, is covered by a test bfs2021 contributed. (#1238)

## Changed

- **The starter's `CoSkyProperties` is bound through its setters.** It and its nested settings were data classes, whose constructors and `copy` the release candidate would have frozen. A setting added later, such as the host a registration publishes, would then have broken code built against the earlier version. Now a setting added later is one more property. (#1257)
- **Secrets stay out of what is printed:** a token's secret, the server's bootstrap token, and a password in its Redis URI. Nothing printed them before, but a log line that did would have leaked them. (#1256)
- **The [security guide](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/security) says who can grant roles:** whoever may write ServiceAccounts, Roles or RoleBindings can give themselves any role, so grant that only to admins. (#1256)

## Upgrading from beta.5

- **Code that constructs `CoSkyProperties`** sets its properties instead, and `copy` is gone:

  ```kotlin
  // before
  CoSkyProperties(namespace = "prod", snapshot = CoSkyProperties.Snapshot(enabled = false))
  // after
  CoSkyProperties().apply {
      namespace = "prod"
      snapshot.enabled = false
  }
  ```

  Applications configured in YAML or properties change nothing.
- Nothing else changes: the gRPC API, the protos, REST, the data in Redis and the properties. `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard come with this release.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on, each replica reads every namespace every second instead. A write then takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.
- **The server does not stop an account from granting itself roles** it may write; see the security guide.
